title: Purchase price allocation
objectives: Answer out loud: How do you calculate goodwill?
Answer out loud: Why is a DTL created?

steps.body: The target's existing book value of equity is replaced.
Assets are written up to fair value (e.g., PP&E, identifiable intangibles).
In a stock deal, the write-up creates a deferred tax liability.
Goodwill = purchase price − book value − write-ups + new DTL. It's the plug.

legend.meaning: Deferred tax liability = write-up × tax rate (stock deal)

blocks.title: Why does an asset write-up create a DTL?
blocks.teaser: In a stock deal, the book value of assets rises (higher future book D&A) but the tax basis doesn't change (no extra tax D&A).
blocks.body:
In a stock deal, the book value of assets rises (higher future book D&A) but the tax basis doesn't change (no extra tax D&A). So future book taxes are lower than cash taxes. That gap is a DTL = write-up × tax rate.

**Interview answer:** "Book basis steps up but tax basis doesn't, so book taxes will be lower than cash taxes. That difference is recorded as a DTL."

blocks.prompt: In a stock deal, PP&E is written up by $100 at a 25% tax rate. What new DTL is created?
blocks.explanation: Book basis steps up but tax basis doesn't, so DTL = write-up × tax rate = $100 × 25% = $25.

blocks.title: Stock deal vs. asset deal?
blocks.teaser: In a stock deal, the buyer acquires the company's shares; the tax basis carries over; buyers inherit all liabilities.
blocks.body: In a stock deal, the buyer acquires the company's shares; the tax basis carries over; buyers inherit all liabilities. In an asset deal, the buyer acquires specific assets; the tax basis steps up to the price paid (more tax-deductible D&A); the buyer can leave liabilities behind. Buyers prefer asset deals; sellers (especially C-corps, facing double taxation) usually prefer stock deals.

blocks.title: What's a 338(h)(10) election?
blocks.teaser: A hybrid: legally a stock deal, but treated as an asset deal for tax, giving the buyer a stepped-up basis.
blocks.body: A hybrid: legally a stock deal, but treated as an asset deal for tax, giving the buyer a stepped-up basis. Only available for certain targets (subsidiaries of corporations, S-corps). Know that it exists.

blocks.title: Where do transaction fees go?
blocks.teaser: M&A advisory and legal fees are expensed (reduce the buyer's equity).
blocks.body: M&A advisory and legal fees are expensed (reduce the buyer's equity). Debt financing fees are capitalized and amortized over the life of the debt.
